literal: Later he held the office of Grand Official of the Outer Capital.
idiomatic: He later served as Grand Official of the Outer Capital.

literal: At his death he was posthumously made Grand General; his posthumous title was Duke Hui.
idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made Grand General, with the posthumous title Duke Hui.

literal: His son Yu, courtesy name Fusheng, inherited.
idiomatic: His son Yu, courtesy name Fusheng, inherited the title.

literal: He held the rank of Defender-in-Chief and was Governor of Xu Province.
idiomatic: He held the rank of Defender-in-Chief and served as Governor of Xu Province.

literal: For corrupt greed he was granted death; the state was abolished.
idiomatic: For corruption he was sentenced to death and the fief was abolished.

literal: The eldest son Bi, courtesy name Yongming, was upright and possessed literary learning; he held the office of Palace Scribe.
idiomatic: The eldest son Bi, courtesy name Yongming, was upright and literary; he served as Palace Scribe.

literal: As heir of the main line, he ought to have inherited the former title.
idiomatic: As heir of the main line he should have inherited his father's title.

literal: His younger uncle, Minister of the Masters of Writing Lü, because of the Yu clan's favor, then seized Bi's princely rank and arbitrarily granted it to his elder brother's son Dan by the same mother.
idiomatic: His younger uncle Lü, Minister of the Masters of Writing, used the Yu clan's favor to strip Bi of his princely rank and give it to his full brother's son Dan.

literal: Thereupon Bi utterly abandoned worldly affairs and pleaded illness to return to his private residence.
idiomatic: Bi then withdrew from public life entirely, citing illness to return home.

literal: Emperor Xuanwu summoned him as Palace Attendant; Bi submitted a memorial firmly declining.
idiomatic: Emperor Xuanwu summoned him as Palace Attendant, but Bi firmly declined in a memorial.

literal: He entered Mount Song, taking a cave for his dwelling, wearing coarse cloth and eating plain food.
idiomatic: He went into Mount Song, made a cave his home, and lived on coarse cloth and plain food.

literal: He died.
idiomatic: He died.

literal: In the first year of Jianyi, his son Huiye petitioned to restore the princely rank.
idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyi his son Huiye petitioned to have the princely rank restored.

literal: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of the State of Situ; his posthumous title was "Wenxian."
idiomatic: In the third year of Yong'an he was posthumously made Director of the Masters of Writing and Duke of Situ, with the posthumous title Wenxian.

literal: Earlier, Bi once dreamed that someone told him: "Your person cannot transmit the hereditary enfeoffment; he who will continue the former title is your eldest son Shaoyuan."
idiomatic: Earlier Bi had dreamed that someone told him, "You yourself will not pass on the hereditary fief; the one who will inherit the former title is your eldest son Shaoyuan."

literal: When Bi awoke he at once told Huiye, and in the end it was as the words had said.
idiomatic: When Bi awoke he told Huiye at once, and in the end it proved exactly as the dream had said.

literal: Huiye in youth was treacherous and shallow, and often associated with bandits and robbers.
idiomatic: In youth Huiye was treacherous and dissolute and often consorted with bandits.

literal: When grown he changed his ways, studied histories and annals, and also wrote rather well, yet was generous and possessed resolve.
idiomatic: As he matured he reformed, studied history, wrote passably well, and became generous and resolute.

literal: He successively held the offices of Minister of Works, Grand Commandant, with special advancement, and concurrently Director of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He rose through Minister of Works and Grand Commandant to special advancement, and concurrently served as Director of the Secretariat and Recorder of the Masters of Writing.

literal: Qi Prince Wenxiang once asked him: "What have you been reading lately?"
idiomatic: Prince Wenxiang of Qi once asked him, "What have you been reading lately?"

literal: He replied: "I often seek the traditions of Yi and Huo; I do not read the books of Cao and Sima."
idiomatic: He replied, "I keep to the stories of Yi Yin and Huo Guang; I do not read the books of Cao Cao and the Simas."

literal: Huiye, because the times were gradually declining, no longer plotted to preserve himself whole.
idiomatic: Seeing the times fade, Huiye no longer strove to preserve himself intact.

literal: He devoted himself only to eating and drinking—three sheep in a day, a calf every three days.
idiomatic: He devoted himself only to feasting—three sheep a day and a calf every three days.

literal: He also once composed a poem saying: "Once I dwelt when the royal way was at peace, / In abundance the host of worthies flourished."
idiomatic: He also once wrote a poem: "Once I lived when the royal way was tranquil, / and hosts of worthies flourished in plenty."

literal: "Now I meet the road of the age obstructed, / Foxes and hares throng in every direction."
idiomatic: "Now the age's road is blocked, / and foxes and hares swarm on every side."

literal: At the beginning of Qi he was demoted and enfeoffed Duke of Meiyang County, Defender-in-Chief with the same ceremony as the Three Dukes, and special advancement.
idiomatic: At the founding of Qi he was demoted to Duke of Meiyang County while retaining Defender-in-Chief with Three-Duke ceremony and special advancement.

literal: While Huiye was at Jinyang he had no social ties; in his usual leisure he compiled the lineages of Wei princely houses, titled Records for Distinguishing Clans in forty scrolls, and it circulated in the world.
idiomatic: At Jinyang he kept no company; in his leisure he compiled the genealogies of Wei princely houses into forty scrolls called Records for Distinguishing Clans, which circulated widely.

literal: His position and eminence were weighty, and because his temperament was unorthodox he was often suspected.
idiomatic: His rank and standing were great, and because his temperament was eccentric he was often suspected.

literal: In the second year of Tianbao, following the emperor to Jinyang, outside the palace gate he cursed Yuan Shao, saying: "You are not the equal of an old woman—carrying the seal on your back to hand it to another; why not smash it to pieces!"
idiomatic: In the second year of Tianbao, on the imperial progress to Jinyang, he cursed Yuan Shao outside the palace gate: "You are worse than an old crone, carrying the seal on your back to give it away—why not smash it to bits!"

literal: "I speak these words knowing I shall die at once, yet how much longer can you last!"
idiomatic: "I say this knowing I shall die at once—but how much longer will you last!"

literal: Emperor Wenxuan heard and killed him, and also beheaded the Prince of Linhuai, Xiaoyou.
idiomatic: Emperor Wenxuan heard of it and had him executed, and also beheaded the Prince of Linhuai, Xiaoyou.

literal: At the execution Xiaoyou was panic-stricken and lost composure; Huiye's expression was calm as ever.
idiomatic: At the block Xiaoyou was panic-stricken; Huiye's face remained serene.

literal: They then cut ice and sank their corpses in it.
idiomatic: Their bodies were then sunk in a hole cut through the ice.

literal: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was rather learned and held the office of Remonstrating Grandee.
idiomatic: Huiye's younger brother Zhaoye was learned and served as Remonstrating Grandee.

literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to visit the south of the Luo, Zhaoye stood outside the Changhe Gate, seized the horse's bridle and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed through.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuangzong was about to travel south of the Luo, Zhaoye stood outside Changhe Gate, seized the bridle, and remonstrated; the emperor avoided him and passed on.

literal: Later the emperor praised and encouraged him.
idiomatic: Later the emperor praised and encouraged him.

literal: He held the offices of Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters, Guards General, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the right.
idiomatic: He served as Attendant of the Yellow Gate in charge of matters, Guards General, and Grand Master of Splendid Virtue on the right.

literal: He died; his posthumous title was Marquis Wen.
idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Marquis Wen.

literal: Yu's younger brother Yan held the office of Grand Master of the Palace.
idiomatic: Yu's younger brother Yan served as Grand Master of the Palace.

literal: His son Fu, courtesy name Boyi, inherited.
idiomatic: His son Fu, courtesy name Boyi, inherited.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Zhuangzong's reign, on behalf of his cousin Huiye he petitioned to seize back the princely rank.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Zhuangzong's reign he petitioned on his cousin Huiye's behalf to recover the princely rank.

literal: He was appointed Governor of Yong Province; his government was harsh and cruel, and officials and people suffered under it.
idiomatic: Appointed Governor of Yong Province, he governed with harsh cruelty that officials and commoners alike resented.

literal: When his wife the Lady Cui bore a son, Li then released the prisoners in the provincial jail—those condemned to death and those in exile or banishment whose cases had not yet been reported to the central offices—and pardoned them all at once.
idiomatic: When his wife Lady Cui bore a son, Li released all prisoners in the provincial jail, including those awaiting execution or exile whose cases had not yet been sent to the capital.

literal: He was transferred to Governor of Ji Province and entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Ji Province, then entered the capital as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: The emperor asked: "I hear that in your province you killed without reason, wrongly condemned many, and also massacred a great number of Buddhist clergy."
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I hear that in your province you killed without cause, wronged many unjustly, and slaughtered a great many monks besides."

literal: He replied: "Your servant in Ji Province could kill on the order of two hundred monks—how is that so many?"
idiomatic: He replied, "In Ji Province I might have killed some two hundred monks—is that really so many?"

literal: The emperor said: "If a single creature does not obtain its proper place, it is as though one were casting it into a moat—how much more when two hundred monks were killed, yet you say it is not many!"
idiomatic: The emperor said, "When even one creature is wronged it is as though cast into a ditch—yet you killed two hundred monks and call that not many!"

literal: Li removed his cap and apologized; he was granted a seat.
idiomatic: Li removed his cap and apologized; the emperor granted him a seat.

literal: He died; his posthumous title was Wei.
idiomatic: He died with the posthumous title Wei.

literal: His son Xianhe in youth possessed moral discipline and successively served as Recorder of the Minister of State.
idiomatic: His son Xianhe in youth had moral discipline and served as Recorder in the Ministry of State.

literal: Minister of State Cui Guang whenever he saw him said: "Recorder Yuan is refined and clear in bearing, graceful and leisurely in deportment—the stuff of a chief minister."
idiomatic: Whenever Minister of State Cui Guang saw him he said, "Recorder Yuan is refined and graceful in bearing—the makings of a chief minister."

literal: He was made Long History of the Eastern Pacification Office of Xu Province.
idiomatic: He was appointed Long History of the Eastern Pacification Office in Xu Province.

literal: The Governor Yuan Faseng rebelled; Xianhe fought and was captured.
idiomatic: When Governor Yuan Faseng rebelled, Xianhe fought and was taken captive.

literal: Faseng took his hand and ordered him to sit together.
idiomatic: Faseng took his hand and ordered him to sit with him.

literal: Xianhe said: "Xianhe and my elder kinsman share one source but different branches—we are all of the bedrock clan. Yet in a morning you rebel with this territory in hand; if Dong Hu were here, could you be without shame in virtue?"
idiomatic: Xianhe said, "Your lordship and I spring from one root, though different branches—we are bedrock of the imperial house. Yet in a morning you rebel holding this land; faced with Dong Hu's brush, could you bear no shame?"

literal: He then refused to sit.
idiomatic: He refused to sit.

literal: Faseng still wished to comfort and persuade him.
idiomatic: Faseng still tried to comfort and persuade him.

literal: Xianhe said: "I can die and become an evil ghost, but I cannot live and be a rebel minister!"
idiomatic: Xianhe said, "I would rather die and be an evil ghost than live as a rebel minister!"

literal: When they were about to kill him, his expression was calm as ever.
idiomatic: When they were about to execute him, his face remained serene.

literal: At the beginning of Jianyi he was posthumously made Governor of Qin Province.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyi he was posthumously made Governor of Qin Province.

literal: The Prince of Ruyin, Tian Ci, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and later was Grand Official of the Inner Capital.
idiomatic: The Prince of Ruyin, Tian Ci, was enfeoffed in the third year of Heping and later became Grand Official of the Inner Capital.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Palace Attendant of the Hall Hu Mo Han selected the wealthy of the western Tiele tribes who also held military households to serve as palace warriors, while greatly taking bribes.
idiomatic: Early in Emperor Xiaowen's reign, Palace Attendant Hu Mo Han drafted wealthy men from the western Tiele who also bore military household status as palace guards, while taking heavy bribes.

literal: The masses were enraged and killed Mo Han and the acting commander of Gaoping, Xi Ling.
idiomatic: The people rose in fury and killed Mo Han and the acting commander of Gaoping, Xi Ling.

literal: Thereupon all the Tiele tribes rebelled.
idiomatic: Thereupon all the Tiele tribes rebelled.

literal: An edict ordered Tian Ci and Attendant of the Masters of Writing Luo Yun to campaign against them.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Tian Ci and Attendant of the Masters of Writing Luo Yun to suppress them.

literal: The vanguard Tiele feigned surrender; Yun believed them.
idiomatic: The Tiele vanguard feigned surrender, and Yun believed them.

literal: Vice Commander Yuan Fu said: "The Tiele show shifting color—fear there will be a change; if we do not prepare now, we shall be plotted against."
idiomatic: Vice Commander Yuan Fu said, "The Tiele look restless—there may be treachery; if we do not prepare now we shall be ambushed."

literal: Yun did not follow.
idiomatic: Yun would not listen.

literal: The Tiele attacked and killed Yun; Tian Ci barely escaped with his life.
idiomatic: The Tiele attacked and killed Yun; Tian Ci barely escaped alive.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Huaishuo Garrison.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand General of Huaishuo Garrison.

literal: For greed and cruelty he was pardoned from death but stripped of office and rank.
idiomatic: For greed and cruelty he was spared death but stripped of office and rank.

literal: At his death Emperor Xiaowen wept at Sizheng Hall; he was posthumously granted his former title, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous title Prince Ling.
idiomatic: At his death Emperor Xiaowen wept at Sizheng Hall; he was posthumously restored to his former title, buried with princely rites, and given the posthumous name Prince Ling.

literal: His son Cheng, courtesy name Wan'an, died as Governor of Qi Province; his posthumous title was Wei.
idiomatic: His son Cheng, courtesy name Wan'an, died as Governor of Qi Province with the posthumous title Wei.

literal: Cheng's son Qinghe was Governor of Eastern Yu Province; when attacked by Liang generals he surrendered the city to them.
idiomatic: Cheng's son Qinghe, Governor of Eastern Yu Province, surrendered his city when Liang generals attacked.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang made him Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Route and Prince of Wei.
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang made him Commander-in-Chief of the Northern Route and Prince of Wei.

literal: When he reached Xiangcheng the court sent troops to punish him; he fled at the sight of the wind.
idiomatic: When he reached Xiangcheng the court sent troops against him; he fled at the first rumor of their approach.

literal: Emperor Wu of Liang reproached him: "Your words match a hundred tongues, your courage is like a mouse's."
idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Liang rebuked him: "Your tongue runs with a hundred voices, your courage is that of a mouse."

literal: He was then transferred to Hepu.
idiomatic: He was then banished to Hepu.

literal: Cheng's younger brother Fan, courtesy name Pu'an, rose from a Yuan clansman of lower rank to Governor of Ying Province.
idiomatic: Cheng's younger brother Fan, courtesy name Pu'an, rose from junior clansman rank to Governor of Ying Province.

literal: Greedy and cruel by nature, the people could not endure his rule and together drove him out; Fan fled to Ping Province.
idiomatic: Greedy and cruel, he drove the people past endurance until they expelled him together; Fan fled to Ping Province.

literal: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Director of the Imperial Clan, and enfeoffed as Baron of Dongyan County.
idiomatic: Later he was made Grand Master of Splendid Virtue and Director of the Imperial Clan, enfeoffed as Baron of Dongyan.

literal: He met disaster at Heyin.
idiomatic: He was killed at Heyin.

literal: Fan's younger brother Xiuyi, courtesy name Shou'an, possessed considerable literary talent.
idiomatic: Fan's younger brother Xiuyi, courtesy name Shou'an, had considerable literary talent.

literal: From a Yuan clansman of lower rank he was gradually promoted to Governor of Qi Province.
idiomatic: From junior clansman rank he was gradually promoted to Governor of Qi Province.

literal: Xiuyi, because Qi Province had repeatedly lost its governors, submitted many memorials firmly declining.
idiomatic: Because Qi Province had repeatedly lost its governors, Xiuyi memorialized again and again to decline the post.

literal: An edict did not permit it but allowed him to establish his headquarters wherever he wished.
idiomatic: The edict refused but allowed him to set up headquarters wherever he chose.

literal: Xiuyi then moved to Dongcheng.
idiomatic: Xiuyi then moved his seat to Dongcheng.

literal: His government was lenient and mild.
idiomatic: His rule was lenient and mild.

literal: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Governor of Qin Province.

literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he memorialized concerning the commoners Xi and the commoner Yu, asking pardon for their former faults and burial in the imperial mausoleum domain.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he memorialized on behalf of the demoted princes Xi and Yu, asking pardon for their past faults and burial in the imperial necropolis.

literal: Empress Dowager Ling edicted: "The grace of gathering for burial is a matter of the supreme will—how may a frontier prince overstep his office and interfere with such a presentation!"
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Ling edicted, "The grace of burial lies with the throne alone—how may a frontier prince overstep his station and meddle in such a petition!"

literal: In the province he accepted many bribes.
idiomatic: In the province he accepted many bribes.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Minister of Personnel.

literal: While holding the scales of appointment he dealt only in bribes; large or small office all had fixed prices.
idiomatic: At the helm of appointments he dealt only in bribes; every office had its price.

literal: At that time the Palace Scribe Gao Ju had an imperial instruction for prior promotion.
idiomatic: At that time Palace Scribe Gao Ju held an imperial instruction for prior promotion.

literal: The post of Shangdang Commandery was vacant; Ju then sought it.
idiomatic: When the post of Shangdang commandery fell vacant, Ju sought it.

literal: Xiuyi had already privately promised it to another; relying on Ju's status he would not give it.
idiomatic: Xiuyi had already promised it privately to another and, relying on Ju's rank, refused to grant it.

literal: Ju spoke with great insolence; Xiuyi ordered his attendants to drag him along.
idiomatic: Ju spoke with great insolence; Xiuyi ordered his attendants to drag him off.

literal: Before the assembled crowd Ju called to Heaven and cried "Thief!"
idiomatic: Before the assembled crowd Ju cried to Heaven, shouting "Thief!"

literal: Someone asked Ju: "In broad daylight in the public hall, how can there be a thief?"
idiomatic: Someone asked Ju, "In broad daylight in the public hall, how can there be a thief?"
